title: VM runtime has no observation or suspension hooks for native debugging
expected_semantics: The canonical VM runtime exposes observation and suspension hooks (safe points, stop conditions, state inspection, replay) so the debugger can target VM execution natively instead of completed reference-runtime runs.
actual_behavior_limitation: mncs-vm (2ab2857) declares debugging, stepping, inspection, snapshot, replay, and observability hooks as owned future work over a minimal SSA-subset engine; no hook surface exists, so all native debugging targets the reference runtime via completed-execution witnesses.
why_capability_matters: Post-hoc witnesses cannot stop, step, or inspect live state; true breakpoints, watches with stops, stepping, and deterministic replay need execution-layer primitives.
current_workaround: Immutable witnesses plus resident sessions, stop sets, watches, and trace replay over bounded runs; live capabilities stay unsupported with pressure pointers.

host_language_code_required.why: No host code involved; the gap is a missing runtime contract.

proposed_primitive_or_semantic_direction: A minimal VM observation contract first (event stream with semantic identity plus safe-point enumeration), then stop/inspect/resume tokens; the debugger's witness/session/stop-set vocabulary is designed to bind to those hooks when they land.
resolution_criteria: The debugger can bind a stop set or watch to a VM execution hook and receive typed stop/inspection events under a documented contract.
